title: Add delta encoding for replay turns array to cut replay JSON size
description:
docs/plan/plan.md section 7.1 documents delta encoding as an intended
optimization for the turns array on long matches ("for very long matches,
the turns array can use delta encoding -- only recording events that
changed from the previous turn") but this is not implemented: engine/replay.go
has no delta logic (grepped for "delta"/"Delta" in engine/replay.go --
only hit is an unrelated Direction.Delta() helper in engine/types.go).
Every turn in a replay is currently stored in full.

Each turn already only records deltas conceptually (moves, spawns,
deaths, captures, energy_collected, energy_spawned, scores -- see the
example schema in section 7.1) rather than full grid state, so the "delta
encoding" here specifically means: don't re-emit unchanged per-player
score/energy totals every turn if they didn't change since the last turn,
and consider omitting turns array entries for structurally uneventful
turns (dedupeable via the existing gzip pass, but true delta encoding
reduces pre-gzip size and, more importantly, parse/reconstruction time in
web/src/lib/replay-data.ts on load).

Concrete scope: measure current uncompressed/gzipped replay size for a
representative 500-turn 4-player match (section 7.1 estimates
200-500KB / 30-80KB), implement delta encoding for the turns array in
engine/replay.go, update the replay format version, update
web/src/lib/replay-data.ts to reconstruct full per-turn state from deltas,
and confirm the replay viewer (web/src/replay-viewer.ts) still renders
identically. Bump replay schema version and update
web/public/replay-schema-v1.json (or introduce v2) accordingly.

Value: smaller payload = faster replay-viewer first paint, especially on
mobile/slow connections, which is the primary way visitors experience
this platform (section 7.3).

title: Expand WASM sandbox opponent roster beyond the initial 6 bots to the other Go/Rust/TS strategy bots
description:
The in-browser WASM sandbox (web/src/pages/sandbox.ts, wasm/) currently
ships only 6 opponent bots: gatherer, rusher, swarm, random, guardian,
hunter (see wasm/Makefile and buildOpponentRow in sandbox.ts). guardian
and hunter are deliberate Go reimplementations of the PHP/Java originals
per docs/plan/plan.md section 13.1 (PHP/Java aren't WASM-practical) -- that
part is correct and should stay as-is.

But per the plan's own language-compatibility table (section 13.1), Go,
Rust, and TypeScript are all "Full" WASM support, and bots/ has 12 more
strategy bots in those languages that are NOT yet in the sandbox:
assassin, phalanx, zone-driver (Rust); coordinator (TypeScript);
economist, farmer, opportunist, siege (Go); plus defender (C#, not
WASM-practical, skip), and kamikaze/pacifist/leader-targeter/nomad/
raider/scout in Java/JS/Python (lower priority -- JS ones ARE
WASM-practical via existing swarm.js pattern, Python needs Pyodide per
section 13.1 and is a separate, heavier lift).

Concrete scope for this bead: add WASM builds + sandbox opponent-select
entries for the 4 Go bots (economist, farmer, opportunist, siege) and 3
Rust bots (assassin, phalanx, zone-driver) using the existing build.sh /
wasm-pack patterns in wasm/bots/{gatherer,rusher}. This takes the sandbox
from 6 to 13 opponents without touching the JS/Python/C# tier, which is a
separate follow-on if wanted.

Value: the sandbox (docs/plan/plan.md section 13.1) is the platform's
zero-deployment onboarding path -- more opponent variety directly
increases how much of the real strategic diversity a newcomer can
practice against before committing to the HTTP ladder.

title: Implement ADR-001 live-tail feed: match worker writes matches/live-tail.json and leaderboard/live-delta.json to R2
description:
Implements the backend half of ADR-001 in docs/plan/plan.md.

cmd/acb-worker already uploads replays/{match_id}.json.gz and
matches/{match_id}.json to R2/B2 immediately after each match (see
uploadReplay in cmd/acb-worker/main.go). Add two more small writes after a
successful match completion:

1. matches/live-tail.json -- rolling list of the last ~50 completed
   matches (match_id, players, winner, final scores, completed_at).
   Append new match, drop oldest once over ~50 entries.
2. leaderboard/live-delta.json -- per-bot rating deltas (bot_id,
   rating_mu delta, matches_played delta) accumulated since the last full
   index build, so the SPA can show "moved up 3 spots" style deltas
   without waiting for the next batch rebuild.

Both objects should be uploaded via the same ARMOR-credentialed R2 client
cmd/acb-worker already holds (no new secrets needed) and served through
the existing Pages Function R2 proxy (web/functions/r2/[[path]].ts) with
Cache-Control: max-age=10, matching the convention already used for
evolution/live.json (cmd/acb-evolver/internal/live/r2.go).

Depends on nothing blocking -- can ship independently of the
cmd/acb-index-builder compile fix, since it's a separate binary
(acb-worker) writing a separate object.

Acceptance: after a match completes, matches/live-tail.json and
leaderboard/live-delta.json in R2 reflect it within the worker's normal
upload latency (seconds, not the ~90 min Pages deploy cycle).

title: Cross-wire critical_moments into clip-maker: auto-suggest clip start/end from the win-probability critical moments
description:
Two features already exist independently but aren't connected:

- Win probability + critical moments (docs/plan/plan.md section 13.2,
  engine/winprob.go ComputeWinProbability): each replay stores a
  critical_moments array (turn, delta, description) for turns where win
  probability shifted >15%.
- Clip maker (web/src/pages/clip-maker.ts): lets a user pick a replay,
  scrub to a start/end turn, and export MP4/GIF in 5 social presets.
  Grepped clip-maker.ts for "critical_moment"/"criticalMoment" -- no hits,
  confirming it's not reading the field at all today.

Currently a user has to already know (or manually scrub to find) the
interesting moment in a match before they can clip it. Wire
clip-maker.ts to read the replay's critical_moments array (already fetched
as part of the replay JSON) and offer one-click "jump to critical moment
N" buttons that set the clip start/end range around that turn (e.g.
critical_moment.turn +/- ~15 turns), the same way the replay viewer's
win-probability graph already supports "click to jump" / "next critical
moment" per section 13.2.

Value: turns "watch a 5-minute replay to find the good part" into "click
the pre-flagged highlight, export it" -- directly serves the platform's
own stated shareability goal (section 13's clip-maker, embed.html,
og-tags.ts) with near-zero new backend work since the data already
exists in the replay.

title: Fix cmd/acb-index-builder compile break: duplicate S3 client declarations across deploy.go, s3.go, cards.go
description:
go build ./cmd/acb-index-builder/... currently fails with redeclaration errors:

  cmd/acb-index-builder/deploy.go:128:75: cfg.PagesProject undefined (type *Config has no field or method PagesProject)
  cmd/acb-index-builder/deploy.go:149:6: uploadFileToR2 redeclared in this block
      cmd/acb-index-builder/cards.go:436:6: other declaration of uploadFileToR2
  cmd/acb-index-builder/deploy.go:320:6: uploadCardsToB2 redeclared in this block
      cmd/acb-index-builder/cards.go:221:6: other declaration of uploadCardsToB2
  cmd/acb-index-builder/s3.go:18:6: S3Client redeclared in this block
      cmd/acb-index-builder/deploy.go:431:6: other declaration of S3Client
  cmd/acb-index-builder/s3.go:47:71: undefined: R2Object
  cmd/acb-index-builder/s3.go:107:20: method S3Client.objectExists already declared at cmd/acb-index-builder/deploy.go:410:20
  cmd/acb-index-builder/s3.go:161:20: method S3Client.downloadObject already declared at cmd/acb-index-builder/deploy.go:424:20
  cmd/acb-index-builder/s3.go:190:6: getR2Client redeclared in this block
      cmd/acb-index-builder/deploy.go:400:6: other declaration of getR2Client
  cmd/acb-index-builder/s3.go:198:6: getB2Client redeclared in this block
      cmd/acb-index-builder/deploy.go:310:6: other declaration of getB2Client
  cmd/acb-index-builder/cards.go:471:19: client.uploadFile undefined (type B2Client has no field or method uploadFile)

deploy.go contains an older stub implementation (uploadObject is a no-op,
downloadObject returns "not implemented", objectExists always returns
false -- see deploy.go lines 409-428) that was never removed when
s3.go / cards.go got a real aws-sdk-go-v2-backed client. Fix: delete the
dead stub types/functions from deploy.go, keep the real implementations in
s3.go/cards.go, add the missing R2Object type and Config.PagesProject
field, then confirm `go build ./cmd/acb-index-builder/...` and
`go vet ./cmd/acb-index-builder/...` are clean.

This binary is the only thing that rebuilds data/leaderboard.json,
data/matches/index.json, and data/bots json files and deploys them to
Cloudflare Pages (see docs/plan/plan.md section 2 and section 8.1).
Because it currently cannot build, the live site
(ai-code-battle.pages.dev/data/leaderboard.json) is still serving a
one-time seed with a 2024-01-18 timestamp and synthetic bot IDs --
confirmed by curling the live endpoint during this audit (2026-07-20).
This blocks ADR-001 in docs/plan/plan.md (live-tail freshness), which
depends on a working batch index builder as its base layer.
